result.title: Detection Instead of Inversion: T1-T2 Microstructure Quantification With Detection Transformers
result.comment: 4 pages, 3 figures, 1 table; For submission to IEEE ISBI 2027; Code: https://github.com/SebastianEndtTHI/t1t2-detr
result.summary: T1-T2 correlation MRI has strong potential to quantify microstructural compartments without imposing a biological model. Traditionally, full T1-T2 spectra per voxel are reconstructed with an ill-conditioned and time-consuming Inverse Laplace Transform. We propose to view this challenge as an object detection task: A Detection Transformer (DETR) takes 64 TI/TE signals and directly predicts a set of compartments specified by T1, T2, and signal fraction. We achieve a mean average precision mAP@10 of 76.8% on simulated data, outperforming both our previous model design (53.8%) and regularized NNLS (66.1%). We show that our DETR approach outperforms NNLS in almost every setting across compartment count, compartmental signal fraction, and SNR. Reconstruction is orders of magnitude faster than NNLS. The results are fully reproducible from our public code: github.com/SebastianEndtTHI/t1t2-detr

AI.brief_summary: 该文把体素级 T1-T2 谱反演改写为集合式目标检测任务，用 DETR 从 64 个 TI/TE 信号直接预测由 T1、T2 与信号占比给出的微结构组分集合，并在仿真数据上以 mAP@10 与速度超过 NNLS。
